summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,200-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 100 views (only a few reach 400-700). The best videos are short, surprising 'sensor/robot does X without Y' ideas about familiar things like robots, clap switches and motion sensors. Weaker videos are generic 'how does X work?' questions about public places or devices (lift, mall door, tap, smoke alarm, touchscreen), which get few views, likes or saves on both platforms.
winningPattern: Hindi videos about a relatable maker project or robot (gyro robot, clap switch, line follower, PIR, mic) with a surprising 'it doesn't do what you think' hook, e.g. 'X doesn't see/hear/think, it only does Y'. Titles are short, use Hinglish, one emoji and #shorts. Posted mainly for Instagram, where shares and saves are highest; YouTube only reacts when the hook is a strong myth-bust (gyro, clap, PIR).
doMore: Use the 'X doesn't do [obvious thing], it only does [surprising thing]' hook in every title and first line
Focus on maker projects and robots (Arduino modules, motors, sensors on a robot) rather than public-place gadgets
Make follow-up parts of winners: gyro robot, clap switch, line follower and PIR each deserve a part 2
Add a save or share trigger in the final line, like 'Save this for your next project' or 'Send to a maker friend'
Keep one clear question or myth per video and test the same top ideas with a stronger YouTube-specific first frame
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' titles on public gadgets (lift, mall door, tap, street light) that have no surprise
Posting near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector, two IR sensor, two tap videos) within days of each other
